title: The human heart
summary: How blood moves through the heart, lungs and body, and what keeps it moving.

nodes.label: Venae cavae
nodes.desc: The two large veins that return blood from the body to the heart.

nodes.label: Right atrium
nodes.desc: The upper right chamber. It receives blood returning from the body.

nodes.label: Tricuspid valve
nodes.desc: The valve between the right atrium and the right ventricle.

nodes.label: Right ventricle
nodes.desc: The lower right chamber. It pumps blood to the lungs.

nodes.label: Pulmonary valve
nodes.desc: The valve at the exit of the right ventricle.

nodes.label: Pulmonary artery
nodes.desc: The vessel that carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

nodes.label: Lungs
nodes.desc: Where blood picks up oxygen and gives up carbon dioxide.

nodes.label: Pulmonary veins
nodes.desc: The vessels that carry blood from the lungs back to the heart.

nodes.label: Left atrium
nodes.desc: The upper left chamber. It receives blood returning from the lungs.

nodes.label: Mitral valve
nodes.desc: The valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle.

nodes.label: Left ventricle
nodes.desc: The lower left chamber. It pumps blood to the whole body.

nodes.label: Aortic valve
nodes.desc: The valve at the exit of the left ventricle.

nodes.label: Aorta
nodes.desc: The body's largest artery. It carries blood from the left ventricle to the body.

nodes.label: Body tissues
nodes.desc: Every organ and muscle that uses the oxygen blood delivers.

nodes.label: Septum
nodes.desc: The muscular wall that divides the right side of the heart from the left.

nodes.label: Heart muscle
nodes.desc: The myocardium: the muscle that makes up the walls of the heart.

nodes.label: Coronary arteries
nodes.desc: Small arteries on the surface of the heart that feed the heart muscle itself.

nodes.label: SA node
nodes.desc: The heart's natural pacemaker, a cluster of cells in the right atrium.

nodes.label: AV node
nodes.desc: The relay between the atria and the ventricles for the heartbeat signal.

nodes.label: Oxygenated blood
nodes.desc: Blood carrying a full load of oxygen.

nodes.label: Deoxygenated blood
nodes.desc: Blood that has given up much of its oxygen to the tissues.

nodes.label: Artery
nodes.desc: Any vessel that carries blood away from the heart.

nodes.label: Vein
nodes.desc: Any vessel that carries blood toward the heart.

nodes.label: Pulmonary circulation
nodes.desc: The loop from the heart to the lungs and back.

nodes.label: Systemic circulation
nodes.desc: The loop from the heart to the body and back.

nodes.label: Double circulation
nodes.desc: Blood passes through the heart twice on each full trip around the body.

misconceptions.label: Single-loop circulation
misconceptions.belief: Blood travels heart, lungs, body, heart in one loop.
misconceptions.correction: There are two loops. Blood returns to the heart after the lungs, and the left side pumps it out again to the body.

misconceptions.label: Arteries defined by oxygen
misconceptions.belief: Arteries always carry oxygenated blood and veins always carry deoxygenated blood.
misconceptions.correction: Vessels are named by direction: arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins toward it. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood and the pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.

misconceptions.label: Artery and vein direction reversed
misconceptions.belief: Veins carry blood away from the heart and arteries carry it back.
misconceptions.correction: It is the other way round: arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins carry it back.

misconceptions.label: The two sides mix
misconceptions.belief: Blood crosses directly between the right and left sides of the heart.
misconceptions.correction: In a healthy heart the septum is a solid wall. Blood only gets from the right side to the left by going through the lungs.

misconceptions.label: The heart feeds on the blood inside it
misconceptions.belief: Heart muscle takes its oxygen from the blood passing through the chambers.
misconceptions.correction: The walls are too thick for that. The heart muscle has its own supply, the coronary arteries, which branch off the aorta.

misconceptions.label: Atria and ventricles swapped
misconceptions.belief: The atria pump blood out of the heart and the ventricles receive it.
misconceptions.correction: Atria receive blood coming into the heart. Ventricles pump it out.

misconceptions.label: Valves push blood
misconceptions.correction: Valves are passive flaps. Pressure opens and closes them, and their job is to stop blood flowing backward.

misconceptions.label: The brain triggers each beat
misconceptions.belief: The brain sends a signal for every heartbeat.
misconceptions.correction: The heart starts its own beats at the SA node. The nervous system only speeds the rate up or slows it down.
